title: Detect TypedAxis duplicates after canonical sort without a full hash set
finding: TypedAxis already had to canonicalize each bounded label sequence by sorting it, but construction first copied all validated labels into a tuple, materialized a complete hash set solely for duplicate detection, then allocated a sorted list and the final retained tuple. At the declared 100,000-label axis ceiling this kept redundant O(n) transient containers even though the mandatory canonical sort makes duplicates adjacent.
primary_claim: TypedAxis now sorts the validated bounded label stream once, detects duplicates by adjacent comparison in that canonical order, and retains the resulting tuple. Duplicate refusal, Fourfold plane typing, axis wire/digest semantics, CSR contracts and Tensor/Fourfold authority remain unchanged.
gardener_decision: Reuse the canonical sort already required by TypedAxis as the duplicate proof and delete the complete transient hash index. Do not introduce a cache, lookup service, alternate axis/block type, planner, store, registry, scheduler or sparse backend.
acceptance: valid TypedAxis construction does not require hashing labels solely for duplicate detection
canonical retained label ordering and wire/digest semantics remain unchanged
